title: A substantial extremal theorem from exponent lattice orderings
objective: Achieve a substantial mathematical advance connected to the smooth-number exponent-lattice observations, with resolving a recognized quantitative problem as the success criterion rather than producing another manuscript. The concrete first target is the worst-case number G_3(n) of distinct monomial initial ideals of a length-n polynomial quotient in three variables, over all fields. Determine its sharp asymptotic growth, or prove an infinite realizable family with a polynomially larger number of orderings than the generic corner-cut scale, together with a consequential general theorem. Explain what algebraic dependencies add to the prime/smooth lattice geometry. First audit the strongest relevant primary literature and the repository's unfinished lattice-shadow work; distinguish a genuinely new theorem from a classical geometric corollary before using it. Success requires a complete uniform proof that settles this extremal question or a substantial recognized part of it, a rigorous consequence for algebraic or geometric complexity beyond restating the count, independently implemented reproducible supporting checks, and an honestly attributed paper. A draft, a bounded priority review, isolated examples, a minor refinement, or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete this goal. If this target is already settled or a route fails, record the evidence and choose a comparably consequential problem still directly linked to the original mathematics; do not silently lower the success criterion. Preserve all existing manuscripts, core smooth-number kernels and auditor, previous research, and the paused ML work. Never send emails, messages to people or other tasks, author queries, or submissions. Publish only explicitly privacy-reviewed research files to the already authorized main branch.
relationship_to_previous_work: New active objective with a higher completion bar. Previous goal records, lattice-shadow candidate, manuscripts and paused ML results are preserved as historical research.

definitions.G_d_n: Maximum number of monomial initial ideals of a colength-n ideal in d variables, over all fields.
definitions.F_d_n: The corresponding maximum for n distinct rational points; F_d(n) <= G_d(n).

success_criteria: Sharp asymptotic growth for G_3(n), or an infinite realizable family polynomially above the generic corner-cut scale together with a consequential general theorem.

A draft, isolated examples, a bounded search, a minor refinement or an unverified novelty claim cannot complete the goal.

continuations.previous_evidence: Commit f2c280c saved the active goal, source comparison and exact family diagnostics.
uniform_proofs: For every monomial basis of a finite algebra supported at one rational point, total degree is at most S=sum_j j*dim(m^j/m^(j+1)). Classical state geometry gives g(I)=O_d((1+S)^(d(d-1)/(d+1))).

For every nonlinear rectangle A_(r,s,F), n=rs, the coordinate moment budgets imply g(I)=O(n^(3/2)*sqrt((r-1)*(s-1)*(r+s-2))). Square rectangles therefore have g(I)=O(n^(9/4)), uniformly over all fields.
The fixed coefficient rule satisfies D*(z+4)-N=0 with D=(1-x)^3*(1-y)^2. Its universal leading monomial x^3*y^2*z is excluded in every initial standard set.
For every r>=8,s>=6, a 23-column ground subset is dependent for the fixed rule but has a unit minor for F=x+y+x^4*y^3. This proves genuine specialization relative to free coefficients.

For every a,b>=1,t nonzero, the embedding F=x+y+t*x^a*y^b in a 2a by 2b rectangle has an explicit coherent standard basis at weight (2,2,3). For a>=4,b>=3 it contains x^3*y^2*z, distinguishing actual initial ideals from the fixed probe.

uniform_proofs: For a finite abelian character table over a splitting field whose characteristic does not divide the group order, every maximal selection of character columns multiplied by independent row parameters to distinct nonnegative block powers has a nonzero generic determinant. Proof: transitive row matroids are uniformly dense; classical matroid partition gives a coefficient which cannot cancel.

For generic graph values above an r by s torus grid, all n=rs distinct canonical monomials with x exponent below r and y exponent below s are independent. Its initial standard sets are exactly ordinary positive n-cuts of the canonical exponent strip.

Any uniform-cut route on at most n*(1+log n)^2 exponent points yielding n^(2+epsilon) standard sets would yield M^(2+epsilon-o(1)) balanced strict halfspace subsets of a general-position three-dimensional configuration. The padding proof keeps M between N and 2N.

continuations.title: Finite gradings obstruct growth from a repeated exponent spacing
continuations.previous_evidence: Commit 69d3cff saved the irreducible-carrier count and its exact wall controls.
uniform_proofs: The lattice generated by support exponent differences in any reduced Groebner basis is independent of term order and gives the universal variable-induced group grading. All monomial basis moments lie in one affine coset. This argument works in every characteristic, including when it divides a finite grading order.

For a rank-two grading lattice of index h, any subcollection of initial standard-set moments has at most 2+C*(area/h)^(1/3) states. Lower-dimensional polygons have at most two vertices. This is a classical lattice vertex bound applied in the correct lattice, not a claimed new lattice theorem.

For I=(x^n,y-G(x)) with nonmonomial support S in degrees 1 through D<n, q=min(S) and h=gcd{j-q:j in S}, the intrinsic grading index is exactly h. All but the pure-x state lie in x<D, giving g(I)<=3+C*n*((D-1)/h)^(1/3).

Consequently (x^n,y-x-c*x^D) has O(n) initial ideals uniformly in the degree, field and nonzero coefficient; prime-power degrees do not escape the bound. A polynomial-graph family with n^(1+epsilon) states must have (D-1)/h=Omega(n^(3*epsilon)).

independent_controls.checks: Direct modular residues and inverse matrices, exact complete cone intervals, every finite-grade component dimension, support-difference index, moment coset, integral relative area and strip bounds. Monomial and free-grading controls included.

A linear-overhead M^(4/3) realization in this class therefore requires D=Theta(n) and bounded h; one repeated offset, including a prime-power offset, gives only O(n) states uniformly. The irreducible-carrier theorem also excludes every fixed-degree carrier. Seek overlapping dependencies escaping both obstructions, in service of the unchanged spatial endpoint G_3(3m)>=G_2(m)^2. A successful linear-overhead realization would give spatial exponent 8/3. No bounded fan screen, classical lattice corollary or unverified novelty claim completes the goal.

continuations.title: Sharp additive prime-power classification and its multiplicative boundary
continuations.previous_evidence: Commit 6653d33 saved the finite-grading lattice bound and its uniform growing-degree obstruction.
uniform_proofs: For any prime power q and every field of its characteristic, a proper finite ideal generated by affine q-linearized polynomials has length q^k. Every global initial ideal is (x_1^(q^a_1),...,x_d^(q^a_d)), sum a_i=k. Classical Frobenius head elimination preserves the ordinary ideal; the final distinct pure-variable heads are an ordinary Groebner basis by the product criterion.

The maximum number of initial ideals in this class is exactly binomial(k+d-1,d-1), over all fields or a sufficiently large finite extension. A generic k-dimensional F_q-linear point space realizes every allocation. Its relevant Moore determinants have distinct determinant monomials, giving a uniform nonvanishing proof.

Every realized allocation has the coefficient-independent canonical strict weight w_i=q^(k-a_i), with heads of weight q^k and all tails at most q^(k-1). The complete weight list has the composition cardinality. The universal reduced basis has at most d times that many polynomials and at most d*(k+2) times that many coefficient entries.

For m input generators of maximum q-degree M, one equal-weight Frobenius reduction gives k<=d*M. At canonical weights every intermediate q-degree is at most M+k. Head elimination and largest-tail-first reduction need at most (m+d)*d*(M+k+1) steps per weight. This yields a polynomial field-operation consequence for fixed d using established reduction, not a new specialized algorithm or field-element bit-cost claim.

The contrast (x^(q^k)-x-1,xy-1) has exactly q^k initial ideals and is reduced over an algebraic closure. One mixed relation escapes the additive logarithmic count but stays linear in quotient length and does not meet the unrestricted power-separation goal.

continuations.title: A sharp unrestricted planar count from dyadic matroid exchanges
continuations.previous_evidence: Commit b1d510a saved the sharp additive prime-power box classification and its multiplicative boundary.
uniform_proofs: For every rank-r matroid with nonnegative integer weights (x,y) satisfying (x+1)*(y+1)<=H, each open-quadrant parametric profile has at most 1+ceil(log2(H))*(r+3*(r^2*H)^(1/3)) canonical states. Repeated weights and nonrepresentable matroids are allowed. Degenerate tied optima are not all counted.

Adjacent greedy swaps give r tokens with monotone coordinates. Cross-dyadic-block swaps are bounded by r*ceil(log2(H)); within each block the coordinate budgets have product at most r^2*H. The elementary primitive-direction estimate K^3<=27*A*B bounds the number of distinct walls. The proof covers simultaneous crossings and all four open quadrants.

Applying the universal ground and residue-matroid dictionary gives g(I)<=1+4*n*ceil(log2(n)) for every planar colength-n ideal over every field.
